safetyClassNote: read-only means: changes no tracked file, remote, or registry. It may update remote-tracking git refs and write logs and receipts under .trellis.

tools.name: gates
tools.description: Runs the root and desktop typecheck and unit tests (and optionally e2e and the desktop build), stops at the first failure, and reports counts and the first failing line instead of the log.

args.name: --only NAMES
args.description: Comma list of steps to run: root-typecheck, root-test, desktop-typecheck, desktop-test, desktop-e2e, desktop-build. With --e2e or --build, the list must name the matching step.

args.name: --e2e
args.description: Also run desktop-e2e under the machine-wide lock; refuses if the lock is held.

args.name: --build
args.description: Also run desktop-build (electron-builder; heavy).

args.name: --clean
args.description: After the run, remove only the allowlisted build outputs (including the root dist; not the installers) and report the bytes freed. A path it refuses, such as a symlink, makes the run fail with exit 1.

args.name: --clean-installers
args.description: After the run, also remove apps/desktop/release, the installers. Run it after release verify has passed: it refuses (exit 1) unless release/desktop-sha256.json exists, names the version in release/beta.json, and records the real SHA-256 of every installer.

args.name: --min-free-gib N
args.description: Raise the free-disk floor above 12 GiB; it can never be lowered.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout, also for a usage error.

output.note: Each step has name, command, cwd, exitCode, passed, reason, ms, rawBytes, counts, firstFailure, and log. A reason is null, TIME_LIMIT, LOG_LIMIT, START_FAILED, NO_SUMMARY, TEST_FAILURES, or NO_TESTS_RAN. clean has removed, refused, freedBytes, and error, and skipped (true only when an interrupt stopped the clean-up). Full logs, with secrets redacted, are in .trellis/gates/<step>.log. A usage error or crash prints {ok:false, exit:2, error} instead.

tools.name: lane-tree
tools.description: Creates, lists, and safely removes the separate working copy for one lane of work; list only reads, and remove is a dry run unless --apply is given.

args.name: create|remove|list
args.description: The subcommand.

args.name: --name SLUG
args.description: create: the lane name, lower-case letters, digits, and dashes.

args.name: --base REF
args.description: create: the base branch (origin/ and refs/heads/ prefixes allowed) or a 40-character commit id, such as origin/release/0.8.0-beta.2. HEAD is not allowed.

args.name: --dest ABS_PATH
args.description: create and remove: the absolute folder of the lane tree.

args.name: --branch NAME
args.description: create: the lane branch (default task/<slug>).

args.name: --modules-from ABS_CHECKOUT
args.description: create: copy node_modules and apps/desktop/node_modules from this checkout, copy-on-write, on macOS only.

args.name: --min-free-gib N
args.description: create: raise the free-disk floor above 12 GiB; it can never be lowered.

args.name: --apply
args.description: remove: delete the folder; without it the command only reports what it would delete. It reads the status, HEAD, and stash again just before it deletes and refuses if they changed. It refuses a lane whose branch was squash-merged and deleted on origin (its commits are not on origin); delete that one by hand.

args.name: --root ABS_DIR
args.description: list: the folder to look in (default: the folder that holds this repository).

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout, also for a usage error.

output.note: Each subcommand puts only the keys marked for it in the result. When --modules-from copies nothing, ok stays true and modulesCopied is false with a modulesNote. A usage error or crash prints {ok:false, exit:2, error} instead.

tools.name: public-scan
tools.description: Scans the added lines of the net diff and of every commit patch, the file paths, commit messages, author names, and the HEAD blob of each added binary file of a branch, and optionally its pull request text, for home paths, session links, emails, secrets (token shapes, passwords inside URLs, and password or auth-token assignments in plain, quoted, and colon forms; ordinary code in one of five strict shapes is not a secret, but a hardcoded fallback after it is; a marker public-scan: allow followed by a kind skips only that kind on its own added line), and private terms, and checks the pull request shape.

args.name: --base REF
args.description: The base to diff against (default origin/release/0.8.0-beta.2).

args.name: --pr-body FILE
args.description: Check the pull request text: alert opener first, at most 300 words, no leaks.

args.name: --terms-file ABS_FILE
args.description: A file outside the repository with one private term per line; findings never print a term. A file with no terms is an error.

args.name: --allow-empty
args.description: Accept a range with no commits or nothing added; without it an empty range exits 1. The output then says it was accepted, never clean.

args.name: --allow-intermediate-binary
args.description: Accept a binary file that a commit added and a later commit removed (it was never scanned); without it that exits 1. The files stay listed as a warning.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout, also for a usage error.

output.note: Each finding has kind, file, line, excerpt, and for a term the termLine in the terms file; a finding on a line that only an earlier commit patch added (it was removed again later) also has commit. A path finding has the file file-path and the position of the path in git diff --name-only as its line. A finding inside a binary file has that file and its line number in the file (a binary file is read line by line). addedLines counts the net diff and patchLines every commit patch. A line over 4000 characters is scanned in overlapping 4000-character windows, never skipped. binaryScanned names the binary files scanned from their HEAD blob (a name that matches a leak pattern is shown as [path withheld]); unscanned lists { file, reason } for a binary file over 5 MiB or unreadable, and makes the exit 1. binaryIntermediate lists the binary files that a commit in the range added or changed but that the net diff does not carry (added and removed again, or put back); they were never read, the exit is 1 unless --allow-intermediate-binary is given (intermediateRefused says whether it was refused), and a name that matches a leak pattern is shown as [path withheld]. binaryNote says that binary content is read as raw bytes and that compressed formats (zip, gz, dmg, docx, pdf streams) are not inspected. It also says that a binary file changed A to B to C inside the range is scanned only at its final (HEAD) version. termsChecked is null when no terms file was given. allowedLines is { count, items } where each item has file, line, and kind (and commit when only a commit patch had the line): the findings that a public-scan: allow marker with a kind skipped, in added lines of the diff only. A file name that matches a leak pattern is shown as [path withheld] in every finding. A usage error or crash prints {ok:false, exit:2, error} instead.

tools.name: release:status
tools.description: Show each release phase as done, todo, or unknown, with a reason.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

output.note: phases lists each release phase as { phase, state, reason }. The tag phase is done only when origin has the tag at the release commit; a tag only this clone holds is todo with (local only) in the reason, and an unreachable origin is unknown. seams (any result, present only when a test seam is active) lists the active test seams; a real run has no seams key.

tools.name: release:preflight
tools.description: Fetch origin, then check branch, sync with origin, and a clean tree. Print the commit.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

args.name: --branch
args.description: NAME. The branch the release must be on.

output.note: checks lists { name, status, detail } for fetch, branch, commit, sync, and clean. seams (any result, present only when a test seam is active) lists the active test seams; a real run has no seams key.

tools.name: release:gates
tools.description: Run the gate commands from the config in order. Stop at the first failure.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --force
args.description: Run the gates again even if a passing receipt exists for this commit.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

args.name: --e2e
args.description: Also run the end-to-end gate.

args.name: --min-free-gib
args.description: N. Raise the free-disk floor; it can never be lowered.

output.note: receipt is the receipt written under .trellis (its seams key lists any test seams in use); ran names the gates run. gate, log, gates, freeGiB, and floorGiB appear only when the step fails, and commit, ran, and receipt only when it passes; the keys in output.optional can be absent. seams (any result, present only when a test seam is active) lists the active test seams; a real run has no seams key.

tools.name: release:dry-run
tools.description: Pack the tarball and run npm publish --dry-run on it. Report size, count, SHA-256, and integrity.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --force
args.description: Run the dry run again even if a passing receipt exists for this commit.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

args.name: --min-free-gib
args.description: N. Raise the free-disk floor; it can never be lowered.

output.note: The tarball, sha256, and integrity are those of the packed file; entries counts every entry in the tarball, bundled files included. log and entry appear only when the step fails (entry names the tarball entry that must never ship). seams (any result, present only when a test seam is active) lists the active test seams; a real run has no seams key.

tools.name: release:publish
tools.description: Print the publish commands for a person to run. Never runs them.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

output.note: A human-only subcommand: it prints commands and runs nothing. Without a terminal the outcome is refused and the exit is 2. commit appears when a dry-run receipt is found. seams (any result, present only when a test seam is active) lists the active test seams; a real run has no seams key.

tools.name: release:hashes
tools.description: Write the SHA-256 of each desktop artifact to the hash file. Every artifact name must contain the release version.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --force
args.description: Replace an existing hash file even when its version or a recorded hash differs.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

output.note: files maps each desktop artifact name to its SHA-256. different, found, and stale appear only when the step fails (found lists the artifacts on disk; stale lists the ones whose name lacks the release version). seams (any result, present only when a test seam is active) lists the active test seams; a real run has no seams key.

tools.name: release:verify
tools.description: Check the registry tag and integrity, an install from the registry, and the desktop hashes.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

args.name: --tarball
args.description: PATH. A local tarball to compare with the registry.

output.note: checks lists { name, status, reason } for dist-tag, integrity, install, and desktop-sha256. seams (any result, present only when a test seam is active) lists the active test seams; a real run has no seams key.

tools.name: release:tag
tools.description: Create the annotated git tag on the checked commit and push that one tag to origin.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

args.name: --commit
args.description: HASH. The full 40-character commit to tag. Needs --branch. The step fetches with --prune and fetches the branch on its own, the tip on origin must equal the tracking ref, then the commit must be an ancestor of exactly origin/<--branch>.

args.name: --branch
args.description: NAME. With --commit (required then): the release branch on origin that must hold the commit; it must match the config branchPattern. Without --commit: the branch the release must be on.

output.note: The tag is created locally with git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null tag -a, then only refs/tags/<tag> is pushed to origin with git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c push.followTags=false push --no-verify --no-recurse-submodules origin refs/tags/<tag>; never a branch, never --force or --tags, and no repository hook runs for the push, the fetches, or the local tag. The step needs a passing gates receipt and a passing verify receipt (same version, on the tagged commit or an ancestor of it), exactly one fetch URL and one push URL on origin, equal, and, under a test seam, a local-path origin. A tag already on origin at another commit is a failure and is never overwritten. With --commit, --branch is required and the branch is fetched on its own, git ls-remote --heads must show a tip equal to the tracking ref, and the commit must be an ancestor of exactly origin/<branch>. existing appears only when the local tag or the tag on origin is at another commit. seams (any result, present only when a test seam is active) lists the active test seams; a real run has no seams key.

tools.name: release:retire
tools.description: Print the npm deprecate and dist-tag commands from the config. Never runs them.

args.name: --json

args.name: --repo

tools.name: release:claims

tools.name: run-node-tests
tools.description: Runs node --test with the given arguments in its own process group under a wall-clock limit, and kills the group past the limit.

args.name: NODE_TEST_ARGUMENTS
args.description: The node --test arguments, without --test.

args.name: BOWERLOOM_TEST_WALL_LIMIT_SECONDS
args.description: Environment variable: lowers the 45 minute limit; it can never raise it.

output.note: Exit 124 on the time limit; the tests it runs may write temp files.
